gfm.appendix:
Current corpus measurements (see the guide for definitions):

| Layer | Exact matches | Remaining differences |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Canonical raw HTML | 672/672 | None in the published corpus |
| Production HTML | 601/672 | 58 HTML5 void-tag spellings, two highlighted fences, two task CSS hooks, nine extension-mode differences |
| Sanitized browser DOM | 627/672 | 32 sanitization-only differences plus 13 presentation/extension-mode differences |

The independent native autolink audit has 53 matches and four intentional differences outside this corpus (GFM-06).

items.title: All 672 published GFM corpus examples match canonical raw HTML
items.expected: Match all 672 pinned examples with their upstream extension flags; measure production extensions and final sanitization separately.
items.disclosure: Canonical raw HTML matches **672/672** published examples with their extension flags, including the two task examples marked disabled upstream. The three original autolink boundary gaps and empty-blockquote serialization are fixed; two old empty-output mismatches were corpus-reader artifacts. Production HTML matches **601/672** and the sanitized browser DOM matches **627/672**, with all remaining corpus differences classified as presentation, extension mode, or sanitization. This is corpus conformance, not full native-engine parity; broader host/email differences are tracked by GFM-06.
items.baselineDisclosure: The pinned GFM corpus matches **582 of 672 exact HTML examples (86.6%)**; **90 deviations** are documented. These include serialization differences in void tags, task-list classes, and highlighted code, as well as differences in reference resolution, tables, nested emphasis, raw HTML, escapes, and extended autolinks. The guide lists the affected specification sections and counts.

items.title: HTML is sanitized after parsing
items.expected: Verify each behavior against cmark-gfm 0.29.0.gfm.13 / markdown-it 15.0.3; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: GFM raw-text tags (including script, style, title, and iframe) are escaped as readable text before browser parsing. All output is then sanitized. Active scripts, event handlers, forms, embedded documents, arbitrary styles, SVG foreign objects, and animation cannot survive as active elements, even where the original parser would preserve them. Static SVG and MathML use a restricted presentation allowlist.
items.baselineDisclosure: HTML is sanitized after parsing. Scripts, event handlers, forms, embedded documents, arbitrary styles, SVG foreign objects, and animation are removed, even where the original parser would preserve them. Static SVG and MathML use a restricted presentation allowlist.

items.title: Math uses Temml's supported TeX notation, not a complete TeX document engine
items.expected: Verify each behavior against cmark-gfm 0.29.0.gfm.13 / markdown-it 15.0.3; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Math uses Temml's supported TeX notation, not a complete TeX document engine. Currency-like dollar pairs are deliberately excluded from math parsing.
items.baselineDisclosure: Math uses Temml's supported TeX notation, not a complete TeX document engine. Currency-like dollar pairs are deliberately excluded from math parsing.

items.title: Code fences display code; Markdown formulas and table cells do not calculate
items.expected: Code and formulas stay display-only in GFM; tasks retain source-edited state and strict Mermaid output remains sanitized.
items.disclosure: Code fences display code; Markdown formulas and table cells do not calculate. Task state is edited in source, rather than through an interactive checklist. Mermaid output is sanitized static SVG with strict security settings.
items.baselineDisclosure: Code fences display code; Markdown formulas and table cells do not calculate. Task state is edited in source, rather than through an interactive checklist. Mermaid output is sanitized static SVG with strict security settings.

items.title: Automatic link recognition has bounded candidates
items.expected: Bound automatic candidate scanning while keeping explicit Markdown links available for complete long addresses.
items.disclosure: Automatic URL recognition scans at most 10,000 characters after a recognized prefix, preserving the existing linkify-it bound. The supplementary GFM email scanner emits only complete candidates of at most 10,000 characters. Remaining text stays visible and existing library matches keep their behavior. Use an explicit Markdown link for a longer address.
items.baselineDisclosure: Automatic URL recognition scans at most 10,000 characters after a recognized prefix, preserving the existing linkify-it resource bound. The remaining text stays visible. Use an explicit Markdown link for a longer address.

items.title: Email gaps are fixed; native autolink differences are intentional
items.expected: Match native email-domain underscores and valid prefixes before plus signs while preserving existing links, Unicode normalization and documented useful recognition.
items.disclosure: Email-domain underscores and valid email prefixes before a plus sign now match the native reference. The separate audit has **53 matching fixtures and four intentional differences**: Sheets retains uppercase WWW links, numeric final email-domain characters, Unicode email hosts with IDNA normalization, and an existing raw HTML anchor instead of producing a nested email link. Canonical corpus conformance remains **672/672**; these native differences are retained policies, not unresolved email-recognition gaps.
items.baselineDisclosure: A separate native audit has **31 matching fixtures and four classified differences** beyond the published corpus. URL-host underscores now follow the last-two-segments rule. Two remaining differences involve email-domain underscores or a valid email prefix before a plus sign. Sheets also retains uppercase WWW links and numeric final email-domain characters where this pinned native version leaves text unlinked. Host validation otherwise comes from linkify-it; the GFM path-ending fixes do not establish complete native autolink parity. Use explicit Markdown links where automatic recognition differs.

items.title: Pinned translator and Temml retain audited notation gaps
items.expected: Verify each behavior against asciimath2tex 1.5.0 / Temml 0.14.0; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: AsciiMath is notation rendering, not evaluation, solving, or a truth check. In 436 pinned upstream cases, 430 translator TeX strings match; four existing differences retain explicit thin spaces omitted by expectations. Two nested-matrix cases have malformed JavaScript expectation strings and different grouping. Temml does not support the arrow command produced by >->> and twoheadrightarrowtail (16 duplicated corpus cases); Sheets now reports these typesetting failures at the formula location. Broader translator/MathML coverage remains FORMAT-1.
items.baselineDisclosure: Formula support follows the pinned asciimath2tex translator, then Temml. This renders notation; it does not calculate, solve, or check the truth of an equality.

items.title: Detectable incomplete formulas now have source-line diagnostics
items.expected: Report missing operands exposed by the pinned parse tree and actual translation/typesetting failures at source locations without replacing upstream grammar or discarding permissive output.
items.disclosure: Sheets warns about synthesized empty denominators, subscripts, exponents and required arguments, bare opening delimiters in required arguments, and unfinished text arguments. Translation and Temml failures are reported separately. Locations cover formula lists, inline/display math and fences, including lists, quotes, tables, Unicode and footnotes. Warnings retain the translated output and Show TeX; later formulas still render. This is not a complete validity or truth checker (AM-05).
items.baselineDisclosure: Incomplete expressions may still render without a diagnostic because the translator is permissive. A rendered formula is not proof of valid input.

items.title: Formula list and Mixed prose modes are explicit and shareable
items.expected: Keep explicitly selected document models stable as prose/Markdown is added; preserve modes across URLs, saved documents, OAuth, downloads documentation and offline reloads.
items.disclosure: AsciiMath mode offers Formula list (asciimath-formulas-v1) and Mixed prose (asciimath-prose-v1). Explicit modes survive edits, sharing, version-2 saves, sign-in returns and offline reloads, and select AsciiMath under Format Auto. Omitted profiles retain the original heuristic; adding Markdown/dollar delimiters can still switch an Auto document. Formula list treats every nonempty line as notation. Mixed prose typesets only delimited/fenced math. Source files contain only text, so reselect the mode when reusing them.
items.baselineDisclosure: A document switches from one-formula-per-line mode to mixed Markdown mode when it contains Markdown structure or math delimiters. Unmarked lines then become prose. Dollar-delimited formulas use AsciiMath rather than TeX in this format.

items.title: Mixed prose inherits the Markdown rendering and sanitization limits above.
items.expected: Verify each behavior against asciimath2tex 1.5.0 / Temml 0.14.0; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Mixed prose inherits the Markdown rendering and sanitization limits above.
items.baselineDisclosure: Mixed prose inherits the Markdown rendering and sanitization limits above.

items.title: Incomplete-input warnings are advisory and preserve permissive notation
items.expected: Leave valid upstream notation and deliberately partial forms available; never claim that rendering or the absence of warnings establishes mathematical validity.
items.disclosure: The adapter inspects the pinned translator tree instead of imposing balanced/matching-delimiter grammar. Standalone operator names, one-sided delimiters, mixed interval brackets, text labels and one-sided limit signs retain upstream interpretation without new warnings. Detectable missing operands receive warnings while still rendering. Other incomplete forms may remain unflagged; no warning means neither a proof of syntax completeness nor a true mathematical statement. Unsupported Temml commands remain typesetting errors (AM-01).
items.baselineDisclosure: Incomplete expressions may still render without a diagnostic because the translator is permissive. A rendered formula is not proof of valid input.

items.title: Statement boundaries and source diagnostics use the pinned upstream parser
items.expected: Preserve valid Numbat 1.24.0 statement boundaries and map structured diagnostic byte spans to original editor positions.
items.disclosure: The adapter now uses Numbat 1.24.0 parser consumption/recovery ranges instead of indentation and trailing-character guesses. Multiline strings, escaped quotes, interpolation, comments, decorators, lists, function parameters, where definitions and semicolons are covered by 25 fixtures checked against the original unmodified WASM. Editor diagnostics map UTF-8 byte spans to actual document lines and UTF-16 columns, retaining related locations from earlier inputs. Lexical-error fallback and local engine-report numbering are disclosed separately in NUM-05.
items.baselineDisclosure: Sheets runs pinned Numbat 1.24.0 through its WASM interpreter. The adapter's statement grouper handles common bracketed and indented continuations, but not every lexical corner of the complete language. A multiline statement's diagnostic attaches to its first source line.

items.title: Terminal commands, a persistent interactive REPL, and a Sheets plot viewer are not provided
items.expected: Verify each behavior against Numbat 1.24.0; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Terminal commands, a persistent interactive REPL, and a Sheets plot viewer are not provided. The interface displays source/result rows, not Markdown prose.
items.baselineDisclosure: Terminal commands, a persistent interactive REPL, and a Sheets plot viewer are not provided. The interface displays source/result rows, not Markdown prose.

items.title: A fresh worker starts for every render, with a 20-second deadline
items.expected: Verify each behavior against Numbat 1.24.0; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: A fresh worker starts for every render, with a **20-second deadline**. Editing or cancellation terminates it; definitions do not persist between renders.
items.baselineDisclosure: A fresh worker starts for every render, with a **20-second deadline**. Editing or cancellation terminates it; definitions do not persist between renders.

items.title: Some short names are predefined units and cannot be redefined
items.expected: Verify each behavior against Numbat 1.24.0; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Some short names are predefined units and cannot be redefined. Currency rates depend on the ECB request/cache; missing or stale rates are disclosed rather than replaced with an invented value. Browser requests now use the official ECB data API; the shared service builds the daily XML required by Numbat, excluding discontinued older series. The original daily XML download blocks cross-origin reads.
items.baselineDisclosure: Some short names are predefined units and cannot be redefined. Currency rates depend on the ECB request/cache; missing or stale rates are disclosed rather than replaced with an invented value.

items.title: Lexical errors stop partial evaluation; formatted engine reports use input-local lines
items.expected: Use whole-document upstream error behavior when tokenization fails and keep editor locations mapped without guessing boundaries in malformed strings.
items.disclosure: If the upstream tokenizer cannot read the document (for example, an unterminated string or unexpected character), Sheets evaluates it as one complete input and reports the lexical error without partial results. Valid-looking text inside a broken string is never guessed to be code. With readable tokens, later statements can run after parse/type/runtime errors. Formatted engine reports retain row-local line numbers; editor annotations use original document positions. Imported-module labels stay in the engine report and are not assigned false editor locations.
items.baselineDisclosure: The previous adapter guessed common continuation boundaries and attached multiline errors to the first line.

items.title: This is a pinned v0.1 draft reference engine, not a compatibility promise for every application using the…
items.expected: Verify each behavior against CalcFile b11ecb44e4a5 (v0.1 draft); separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: This is a pinned **v0.1 draft** reference engine, not a compatibility promise for every application using the same file extension. Functions, units, and locale behavior are limited to that draft.
items.baselineDisclosure: This is a pinned **v0.1 draft** reference engine, not a compatibility promise for every application using the same file extension. Functions, units, and locale behavior are limited to that draft.

items.title: ECB decimal rate environment supplied to CalcFile
items.expected: The adapter supplies the pinned engine with validated decimal-string ECB rates only when actual calculations need external data. Online, cached/offline, missing, malformed and cancelled requests have deliberate results; the 37-case corpus remains unchanged.
items.disclosure: The shared service reads the browser-accessible official ECB data API and builds a validated daily XML snapshot while preserving decimal rate text and the latest publication date. Discontinued older series are excluded. CalcFile now supplies validated decimal-string ECB rates with their publication date, fetching only when the engine reports missing external data. Supported EUR-base conversions work online or with a valid cache. Refresh failures disclose older cached rates; malformed or unavailable data keeps source-line diagnostics. Cancellation discards late responses without cache writes. The original 37 required upstream conformance cases still pass. Pair/currency and rate-snapshot boundaries remain under CF-05.
items.baselineDisclosure: All 37 required upstream conformance cases pass, including cases with supplied exchange rates. The **Sheets UI supplies no currency-rate environment** to CalcFile, so cross-currency conversion reports missing external data.

items.title: Auto detection deliberately does not select CalcFile from ambiguous prose
items.expected: Verify each behavior against CalcFile b11ecb44e4a5 (v0.1 draft); separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Auto detection deliberately does not select CalcFile from ambiguous prose. Choose it explicitly. Raw HashBin text lacks a filename and uses Auto unless the format is overridden or stored in a Sheets envelope.
items.baselineDisclosure: Auto detection deliberately does not select CalcFile from ambiguous prose. Choose it explicitly. Raw HashBin text lacks a filename and uses Auto unless the format is overridden or stored in a Sheets envelope.

items.title: Output is a line calculator with headers and text, not a Markdown renderer or an interactive spreadsheet
items.expected: Verify each behavior against CalcFile b11ecb44e4a5 (v0.1 draft); separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Output is a line calculator with headers and text, not a Markdown renderer or an interactive spreadsheet. Incomplete input can remain incomplete while typing; aggregates reject incompatible types.
items.baselineDisclosure: Output is a line calculator with headers and text, not a Markdown renderer or an interactive spreadsheet. Incomplete input can remain incomplete while typing; aggregates reject incompatible types.

items.title: This is a JavaScript spreadsheet subset, not Emacs Org, Babel, or the complete Emacs Calc language
items.expected: Verify each behavior against Emacs numeric fixture oracle; documented Calc subset; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: This is a JavaScript spreadsheet subset, not Emacs Org, Babel, or the complete Emacs Calc language. Emacs Lisp formulas are explicitly unsupported.
items.baselineDisclosure: This is a JavaScript spreadsheet subset, not Emacs Org, Babel, or the complete Emacs Calc language. Emacs Lisp formulas are explicitly unsupported.

items.title: Remaining Org target syntax, numeric modes, iteration and native layout are incomplete
items.expected: Verify remaining target syntax, iteration, remote indirection/file inputs, symbolic and duration Calc results, and native layout in separate reference-backed slices.
items.disclosure: Numeric named bindings, same-document remote cells/ranges and Emacs Calc default/explicit numeric modes work (ORG-09). The explicit Emacs-order profile supplies row-major sorted columns, protected fields, sorted field formulas and duplicate-target rejection; Legacy retains source-order links. Target ranges, relative targets in Emacs order, dynamic remote indirection, A1 remote notation, cross-file/ID references, iteration, property/external or nonnumeric bindings, Calc symbolic/complex/unit/date/duration results and exact Emacs display-width/full export layout remain unsupported. Header groups and numeric column alignment are supported (ORG-12); rich table-cell markup, captions, column groups, native width handling and export omission of calculation marker rows/columns remain incomplete. Remote and Calc failure diagnostics retain the affected cell instead of native symbolic or #ERROR text. Numeric conditional formulas and comparisons are supported (ORG-10), while vector/symbolic conditions and comparisons, logical operators and ternary syntax remain unsupported. Thousands grouping, including grouped currency display, is not provided. ;%.2f controls decimal places and a literal dollar prefix is possible, but it does not add grouping. Cross-document inputs still require duplicated constants or tables until FILE-1. UTF-8 BOM and CRLF files parse through normalized input; shared/editor source remains exact, while recalculated source uses LF without a BOM.
items.baselineDisclosure: Named fields, remote tables, iteration modes, arbitrary Calc syntax, and exact Emacs display-width alignment are not implemented. Formulas execute in order, rather than iterating until results converge.

items.title: Surrounding prose supports basic headings, lists, emphasis, and links, rather than the full Org…
items.expected: Verify each behavior against Emacs numeric fixture oracle; documented Calc subset; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Surrounding prose supports basic headings, lists, emphasis, and links, rather than the full Org application/export environment. Numeric table calculations use a project-owned Emacs Calc subset (ORG-09), not the complete Calc language or a dimension-checked physical modeling language. Cell text is read as Calc input: empty fields become zero and are dropped from ranges unless E keeps them as nan; nonnumeric text is symbolic in Calc and produces a diagnostic unless N converts it with Emacs number parsing.
items.baselineDisclosure: Surrounding prose supports basic headings, lists, emphasis, and links, rather than the full Org application/export environment. Numeric table calculations use the constrained mathjs evaluator; this is not a general dimension-checked physical modeling language. Ranges skip nonnumeric cells unless numeric coercion is requested.

items.title: Recalculation updates the preview
items.expected: Verify each behavior against Emacs numeric fixture oracle; documented Calc subset; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Recalculation updates the preview. The editor retains the original source until you copy recalculated source and paste it. Out-of-range references report diagnostics instead of creating cells. Independent Emacs comparisons cover supported numeric fixtures and exclude the intentional Lisp-error example. Preview cells cannot be edited directly, marked as inputs, or given per-cell notes. Org has no goal seek or what-if tool; Calca’s scalar solver is a separate format and does not solve Org table cells. These are UI-1 feature requests, not native recalculation fixes.
items.baselineDisclosure: Recalculation updates the preview. The editor retains the original source until you copy recalculated source and paste it. Out-of-range references report diagnostics instead of creating cells. Independent Emacs comparisons cover supported numeric fixtures and exclude the intentional Lisp-error example.

items.title: Numeric named bindings and marked-row selection match Emacs fixtures
items.expected: Supported numeric binding and source-ownership cases match committed independent Emacs results and editor round-trip checks.
items.disclosure: The first name row supplies column aliases; field markers name adjacent fields; numeric table parameters and file constants provide reusable inputs. Precedence, duplicate behavior, pre-pass field snapshots, scientific notation, ranges and marked-row selection are checked against Emacs. Named fields can be targets; column targets stay numeric. Remaining binding and evaluation features stay under ORG-02.
items.baselineDisclosure: Named fields and columns, table parameters and file constants were not implemented; metadata rows could be recalculated as data.

items.title: Literal Org blocks no longer run formulas or install constants
items.expected: Supported numeric binding and source-ownership cases match committed independent Emacs results and editor round-trip checks.
items.disclosure: Active tables and constants are discovered through the Org AST. Source/example/export blocks remain escaped literals and comment blocks are omitted. Their apparent formulas and constants do not affect calculations. Quoted formula strings retain their literal dollar signs. Exact source is preserved in editor shares and downloads.
items.baselineDisclosure: The line scanner could treat a table in a source block as executable spreadsheet input.

items.title: Explicit Emacs order matches supported native scheduling and duplicate-target rejection
items.expected: Match the supported successful and rejected native reference documents while preserving Legacy links and the explicit profile migration contract.
items.disclosure: The org-emacs-v1 profile sorts stored targets lexically, applies columns row by row with field protection, then applies sorted field formulas. Duplicate numeric/named/boundary targets reject the formula line before writes. Only the first stored TBLFM line is active, allowing preceding blank lines. Existing unprofiled links and version-1 saves retain Legacy source order. Target ranges, relative targets and full dependency solving remain outside this supported slice.
items.baselineDisclosure: Formulas always ran in source order, column by column; explicit field targets were not protected and duplicate targets overwrote earlier results.

items.title: Same-document remote references read current pass state without recursive evaluation
items.expected: Match the supported successful and rejected native reference documents while preserving Legacy links and the explicit profile migration contract.
items.disclosure: remote() reads numeric cells/ranges or named numeric fields from active named tables in the same source document. Table names are case-insensitive and first-match wins; field/column aliases remain case-sensitive. References use current document-order pass state and never recursively recalculate dependencies. Blank-separated tables remain distinct and literal blocks cannot supply data. Missing/unsupported/out-of-range references report source-line diagnostics and retain the cell. Dynamic names, A1 notation, relative remote addresses and file/ID lookup remain unsupported.
items.baselineDisclosure: Remote table references were unsupported; adjacent blank-separated tables could be merged by the structural parser and a later table could be missed.

items.title: Formulas use Emacs Calc default modes, exact integers and Calc display
items.expected: Match Emacs org-calc-default-modes (degrees, 12-digit internal precision, (float 8) display, no fraction preference), Calc precedence, exact integers and the supported mode letters in both calculation modes.
items.disclosure: Formulas follow a DOM-free Emacs Calc subset in both Legacy and Emacs order: degree angles, 12 internal digits and an 8-significant-digit float display, exact integers, trailing-point floats (5.), Calc scientific-notation thresholds, multiplication binding tighter than division (10/4*2 is 1.25), Calc function names (arcsin, not asin) and Calc exact trigonometric/logarithm special cases. Mode letters p, n, f, s, e, D, R, F, E, N and L, one printf conversion (%d, %f, %e or %g, applied to the displayed value as Emacs does) and the table % format parameter are supported. Symbolic results, complex numbers, infinities, units, dates, strings, durations (T, t, U), symbolic mode S and unit mode u produce source-line diagnostics and retain the cell instead of native symbolic or #ERROR text. No advisory hint warns about mixed multiplication/division; parenthesize the intended division explicitly.
items.baselineDisclosure: Formulas used JavaScript/mathjs numbers in radians with 12 significant display digits, standard precedence and mathjs function names. Mode letters other than N and %.Nf were silently ignored, and %.Nf formatted the unrounded double, so sin(30), 1/3 and 2^0.5 showed -0.988031624093, 0.333333333333 and 1.41421356237 instead of 0.5, 0.33333333 and 1.4142136.

items.title: This is a compatible subset implemented with constrained mathjs, not the original commercial Calca…
items.expected: Verify each behavior against public Calca reference; licensed-app verification still needed; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: This is a compatible subset implemented with constrained mathjs, not the original commercial Calca application or a complete mathjs shell. Object access, arbitrary JavaScript, imports, ranges, and unlisted functions are rejected.
items.baselineDisclosure: This is a compatible subset implemented with constrained mathjs, not the original commercial Calca application or a complete mathjs shell. Object access, arbitrary JavaScript, imports, ranges, and unlisted functions are rejected.

items.title: Equation solving supports real scalar linear and quadratic polynomials with numeric coefficients
items.expected: Verify each behavior against public Calca reference; licensed-app verification still needed; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Equation solving supports **real scalar linear and quadratic polynomials with numeric coefficients**. Symbolic answers, unit-valued equations, general simultaneous systems, function inversion, higher powers, unknown denominators, and transcendental equations are unsupported.
items.baselineDisclosure: Equation solving supports **real scalar linear and quadratic polynomials with numeric coefficients**. Symbolic answers, unit-valued equations, general simultaneous systems, function inversion, higher powers, unknown denominators, and transcendental equations are unsupported.

items.title: Equation selection and bounded connected-constraint checks
items.expected: Verify each behavior against public Calca reference; licensed-app verification still needed; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Legacy and Structured blocks prioritize explicit assignments and the latest usable equation, possibly skipping unsupported or underdetermined relations. Scoped definitions checks all connected real scalar relations against candidate roots and reports conflicts; it is not a general simultaneous-system solver. Derived answers are not stored as assignments. Expressions depending on multiple or no roots report diagnostics; query the unknown directly. Identities report infinitely many solutions. Complete native-app equation selection and conflict behavior still needs verification.
items.baselineDisclosure: Explicit assignments take priority. Queries look backward for the most recent usable equation and may skip unsupported or underdetermined relations. This is not a simultaneous-equation consistency checker. Derived answers are not stored as assignments. An expression depending on multiple or no roots reports a diagnostic rather than choosing a root; query the unknown directly instead. Identities report infinitely many solutions rather than selecting an answer.

items.title: Definition semantics and native-app verification
items.expected: Verify each behavior against public Calca reference; licensed-app verification still needed; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Legacy and Structured blocks allow reassignment, share one document context, and use assignment-time values for resolved numeric definitions. Scoped definitions (calca-scopes-v1) retains the first visible definition, treats repeated definitions as constraints, resolves deferred dependencies and function free variables at query time, and scopes definitions/relations to headings and descendants. Child definitions cannot shadow inherited names. The public heading example is covered; child redefinition, deferred binding, conflict presentation, and Setext rules are explicit Sheets policies pending licensed-app comparison. State resets on every render.
items.baselineDisclosure: Numeric definitions use assignment-time values; unresolved definitions use current values when queried. Reassignment is allowed, headings do not create scopes, and state resets on every render. These behaviors differ from Calca.

items.title: Results use floating-point arithmetic with up to 12 significant displayed digits
items.expected: Verify each behavior against public Calca reference; licensed-app verification still needed; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Results use floating-point arithmetic with up to 12 significant displayed digits. Scoped relation checks allow 64 machine epsilons of relative error; solved unknowns use arithmetic magnitude, including terms lost to cancellation, without an absolute floor. These checks are numerical, not exact proofs. Expressions allow 4,000 characters and 1,000 syntax nodes. Legacy and Structured blocks allow 256 equations; Scoped definitions allows 256 definitions/relations together, with dependency/relation-expansion depth 32 and bounded query work. This numerical policy is not verified native Calca equivalence.
items.baselineDisclosure: Results use floating-point arithmetic with up to 12 significant displayed digits. Expressions are limited to **4,000 characters and 1,000 syntax nodes**, documents to **256 equations**, with additional bounds on definition expansion.

items.title: Calculation and literal Markdown block isolation
items.expected: The explicit Sheets structured-block profile isolates literal Markdown input, executes supported calculation blocks, and retains original source locations. Unprofiled documents keep legacy behavior.
items.disclosure: Structured blocks (calca-blocks-v1), also included in Scoped definitions (calca-scopes-v1), uses parsed Markdown boundaries: only calca-labelled fences, indented code, and standalone paragraph arrow expressions calculate. Literal language/unlabelled fences, TeX, Mermaid, inline code/math, headings, links, and HTML do not run as calculations. Legacy remains the default for unprofiled URLs and version-1 saved documents. This resolves Markdown block isolation in the explicit profile; it does not implement Calca’s complete input grammar.
items.baselineDisclosure: Every fenced or indented code block is calculation input, regardless of its language label. Literal code, math, or Mermaid fences can therefore produce calculation diagnostics. Arrow answers replace text in the preview; the editor source is retained. Built-in unit/constant names can conflict with unknown names.

items.title: Sheets embeds a pinned upstream calculation/rendering engine, not Hurmet's rich-text editing application
items.expected: Verify each behavior against Hurmet 24abefdaecbc; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Sheets embeds a pinned upstream calculation/rendering engine, not Hurmet's rich-text editing application. Interactive drawing tools and live spreadsheet editing are outside this shell; tables and calculations are edited as source.
items.baselineDisclosure: Sheets embeds a pinned upstream calculation/rendering engine, not Hurmet's rich-text editing application. Interactive drawing tools and live spreadsheet editing are outside this shell; tables and calculations are edited as source.

items.title: Every render gets a fresh worker with a 20-second deadline
items.expected: Verify each behavior against Hurmet 24abefdaecbc; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Every render gets a fresh worker with a **20-second deadline**. There is no persistent calculation session across edits.
items.baselineDisclosure: Every render gets a fresh worker with a **20-second deadline**. There is no persistent calculation session across edits.

items.title: Remote-data fetches follow upstream behavior and browser CORS rules
items.expected: Verify each behavior against Hurmet 24abefdaecbc; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Remote-data fetches follow upstream behavior and browser CORS rules. Fresh ECB currency rates and uncached remote data need a connection; ordinary calculations can use downloaded offline assets. HTML exports contain finished static output, rather than a live Hurmet interpreter.
items.baselineDisclosure: Remote-data fetches follow upstream behavior and browser CORS rules. Fresh ECB currency rates and uncached remote data need a connection; ordinary calculations can use downloaded offline assets. HTML exports contain finished static output, rather than a live Hurmet interpreter.

items.title: This is a project-owned core JavaScript engine, not Python Beancount or a full query environment
items.expected: Verify each behavior against Beancount 3.2.0 / beanquery 0.2.0; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: This is a project-owned core JavaScript engine, not Python Beancount or a full query environment. Includes, plugins, advanced options, combined costs, merge markers, lot cost/quantity interpolation, and multi-commodity interpolation across multiple missing amounts remain unsupported. Per-unit/total costs, date/label selectors, and six booking methods are supported; see BEAN-07/08.
